questions.question_text: You receive an ARM template that creates a storage account. Which property in the template ensures that the storage account is deployed with a specific redundancy type?
questions.explanation: The sku.name property defines the SKU, which includes the redundancy configuration as described in the Azure documentation.

questions.question_text: Your existing ARM template creates a virtual machine. To add an Azure managed disk as a separate resource, which modification should you make?

options.label: A
options.text: Add a new resource with type "Microsoft.Compute/disks" to the resources array.

options.label: B
options.text: Modify the existing virtual machine resource and add a "disks" property.

options.label: C
options.text: Insert a new "dependsOn" entry for the disk resource.

options.label: D
options.text: Change the "apiVersion" of the virtual machine resource to a newer version.

questions.explanation: To create a managed disk, you add a separate resource of type Microsoft.Compute/disks, as explained in the Azure documentation for resource types.

questions.question_text: You have an ARM template in JSON format and want to convert it to Bicep. Which Azure CLI command performs this conversion?
questions.explanation: The az bicep decompile command converts an ARM template to Bicep, according to the Azure CLI documentation.

questions.question_text: When deploying a resource that requires a secret value, such as a SQL server admin password, which parameter type should you use in a Bicep file?
questions.explanation: Bicep supports secureString parameters that are encrypted in the template and not exposed in logs, as detailed in the Azure documentation.

questions.question_text: To export a deployment that created a resource group, storage account, and virtual machine as an ARM template using Azure CLI, which command should you run?

options.label: A
options.text: az deployment group export --resource-group MyRG --template-file exported.json

options.label: B
options.text: az deployment group create --template-file template.json --output json

options.label: C
options.text: az deployment group export --name MyDeployment --resource-group MyRG --output json

options.label: D
options.text: az deployment group show --resource-group MyRG --query "properties.template" > exported.json

questions.explanation: The az deployment group export command creates a template file representing the deployment, as described in the Azure CLI reference.
